summary: POC scoping focused on defining latency & throughput SLOs for Evora's chat assistant use case. We covered success criteria (TTFT and TPOT p95/p99 targets), workload sizing (QPS, prompt length, concurrency), measurement plan (bench harness, synthetic vs trace-driven tests), and pilot timeline. Evora is leaning toward Redwood Dedicated if latency targets require reserved capacity, but will run hosted baseline benchmarks first. Next steps: exchange traces, run benchmarks, and review results before formal SOW.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-05
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Kim (Evora CTO), Maya Lopez (Evora ML Eng), Ravi Singh (Evora Infra)

[00:00:00] Samir (Redwood): All right folks, thanks for joining. I'm Samir, AE on the account, and Priya will run the technical bits. Quick agenda — align on success criteria for the POC, nail down the latency SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), workload sizing, and agree a measurement plan and timing.

[00:00:30] Daniel (Evora): Sounds good. We're short on time today but we want to get concrete numbers. Our product is a customer-facing chat assistant, mixes short prompts and a few longer context responses. Main ask: keep perceived latency low under peak.

[00:01:10] Priya (Redwood): Great — can you give us ballpark traffic? QPS, concurrency, typical prompt lengths, and any special constraints like on-prem or strict KMS?

[00:01:35] Maya (Evora): Peak is about 120 qps now for the chat endpoint, tail at maybe 200 qps during campaigns. Average prompt tokens ~40, median output ~60 tokens; but we have longer flows up to 300 tokens for multi-step generation. We need SOC2 level controls, SSO, and prefer traffic not leave our VPC for sensitive requests.

[00:02:10] Ravi (Evora): Also, we care about TTFT for the first token — our UX shows loading indicator until the first word — so TTFT impacts UX more than raw throughput. But cost is also a factor, so if dedicated GPUs reduce per-token cost (or improve tail), that'd be considered.

[00:03:00] Samir (Redwood): Thanks — that helps. Priya, can you describe how Redwood thinks about TTFT and TPOT and what benchmarks we usually run?

[00:03:22] Priya (Redwood): Sure. Quick defs: TTFT is Time To First Token — latency from request arrival to the first output byte/token. TPOT we often shorthand as time-per-token (average per-token generation time) — important for long responses. For SLOs we usually target both p95 and p99 for each metric across representative prompt sets. Typical baseline for similar customers: TTFT p95 ~<200ms, p99 ~<400ms on a Hosted profile for short prompts; TPOT p95 ~10-20ms/token, p99 ~25-40ms/token depending on model-size and quantization.

[00:04:10] Daniel (Evora): Those numbers look promising. Our internal goal is perceived latency p95 under 300ms for the short chat path; p99 under 600ms ideally. For longer flows, it's more about consistent per-token times so we don't have long stalls.

[00:04:45] Priya (Redwood): OK so we should agree representative prompt sets: 1) short chat (prompt ~20-50 tokens, response up to 60 tokens), 2) medium instruction (100-200 tokens output), 3) long code/assistant flow (200-500 tokens). We'll run trace-driven tests using your production traces and some synthetic stress tests at 1.5x peak.

[00:05:20] Maya (Evora): For the trace export, what's the format you need? We can supply a 24-hour sample with request timestamps, token counts, and a few metadata fields.

[00:05:40] Priya (Redwood): CSV or NDJSON works — we need request timestamp, prompt length (tokens), desired max output tokens, and a sample prompt. We'll provide a runbook for scrubbing PII.

[00:06:05] Ravi (Evora): Policy-wise, can we run the initial bench on Hosted but route sensitive requests to a Private deployment later? We're concerned about data residency and KMS.

[00:06:30] Samir (Redwood): That's a common pattern. For POC we'll recommend a staged approach: Hosted baseline to validate latency and throughput with your traces (fastest to launch), then optionally spin up a Dedicated pool or Private deployment if tail or KMS needs push you there. We'll show delta in costs and performance.

[00:07:05] Daniel (Evora): What's the measurement plan — how do you compute p95/p99? Are you aggregating per-request TTFT or per-connection? Also, how do you handle streaming vs non-streaming endpoints?

[00:07:30] Priya (Redwood): We'll measure per-request TTFT at the API ingress point — timestamp when request received and timestamp of first byte emitted by the model stream. For non-streaming we use first token emitted similarly. We'll capture per-token times for TPOT by looking at generation intervals across the sequence (for streaming clients). We'll compute p50/p95/p99 across the test window. For trace-driven tests we'll replay same inter-arrival pattern and measure under steady-state and burst conditions.

[00:08:25] Maya (Evora): What about batching effects? Our traffic has bursts where batching could help but spikes where latency matters.

[00:08:45] Priya (Redwood): Good point. Redwood runtime does continuous batching; it trades a small TTFT cost for better throughput. For the POC we'll run scenarios toggling batching and target SLOs: 1) low-latency mode (minimal batching), 2) cost-optimized mode (aggressive batching), and 3) a mixed policy with dynamic routing by latency window. We'll capture how p95/p99 shift.

[00:09:30] Daniel (Evora): For model sizes, what are reasonable picks? We're evaluating both a smaller 7B open model and a 13B or 70B variant for higher quality.

[00:09:50] Priya (Redwood): We'll include the two model classes in the bench. Expect TTFT/TPOT to scale up with model size. Quantized 13B on A100 or T4-class hardware often gives good TPOT; 70B will be slower unless you use vRAM-optimized hardware and dedicated pools. We'll quantify token cost and latency tradeoffs.

[00:10:30] Samir (Redwood): To be concrete, let's propose initial SLO targets for the POC to validate: short chat (prompt <50 tokens, response <=60 tokens): TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms; TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token, p99 <= 35ms/token. Medium flows: TTFT p95 <= 400ms, p99 <= 700ms; TPOT p95 <= 25ms/token. Long flows: focus on TPOT stability, p95 <= 30ms/token. Does that align with Evora expectations?

[00:11:10] Daniel (Evora): That's close. Can we relax p99 on Hosted for the POC and treat Dedicated as the option to meet stricter p99? So Hosted: p99 +20-30% buffer. Dedicated: aim to meet the tighter p99.

[00:11:40] Priya (Redwood): Absolutely — part of the POC is to show the delta. We'll run Hosted baseline, then a Dedicated run with pinned instances to show reduced variance and improved tail. We'll also measure the impact of KV cache warm vs cold on sequential flows — that can affect TTFT for follow-up turns.

[00:12:20] Ravi (Evora): What tooling will we get to reproduce these? Are you giving a harness and dashboards?

[00:12:40] Priya (Redwood): Yes — we'll provide a benchmark harness (open repo) that replays traces, a waveform for token timings, and dashboards that show TTFT, token histogram, TPOT, QPS, and resource utilization. We'll also share scripts to run on both Hosted and Dedicated profiles and a standard JSON output of the results.

[00:13:10] Maya (Evora): On measurement windows — how long do you run each test to get stable p99s?

[00:13:30] Priya (Redwood): Typically 10-30 minutes for steady-state with multiple runs; for p99 stability under burst we recommend at least 30 minutes or a longer 1-2 hour run during a simulated campaign. For initial POC we can do 3 x 20 minute runs per scenario and aggregate.

[00:14:05] Daniel (Evora): How do you ensure clock sync and consistent timestamps when we run in our environment?

[00:14:20] Priya (Redwood): The harness uses client-side and server-side timestamps: client records request send time; Redwood logs server receive and first-byte timestamps. We'll use NTP-synced machines and correlate by request ID. We'll also include a warm-up phase to avoid cold-start noise.

[00:15:00] Samir (Redwood): Let's talk success criteria beyond raw latency — what decisions will Evora make after the POC?

[00:15:20] Daniel (Evora): We'll use results to decide whether to: 1) adopt Hosted for production with some routing rules, 2) commit to Dedicated for steady performance, or 3) move to Private for KMS/residency. Also need an ROI calc on per-token cost vs infra cost.

[00:16:00] Samir (Redwood): We'll provide a cost delta analysis as part of the results. Any compliance or security checks we should prep for?

[00:16:18] Ravi (Evora): SOC2 report, SSO (SAML), RBAC controls, and KMS integration (customer-managed keys). Also audit logs retention for 90 days.

[00:16:40] Priya (Redwood): Redwood supports those. For Private/Dedicated we can integrate your KMS and provide audit logs. We'll attach the security pack and SOC2 docs.

[00:17:00] Maya (Evora): For the bench, do you need sample prompts with PII? We can scrub, but some context is needed to mimic tokenization and length distribution.

[00:17:20] Priya (Redwood): Scrubbed, representative prompts are fine; include token counts and mark any flows where context windows span many turns.

[00:18:00] Daniel (Evora): On metrics, can you expose CPU/GPU utilization + queue depth so we can understand if latency is queuing or model time?

[00:18:20] Priya (Redwood): Yes — our dashboards include GPU utilization, batch sizes, queue latencies, and per-request traces. We'll share an example dashboard.

[00:19:00] Samir (Redwood): Let's map timeline: Samir to send SOW draft and pricing by Monday 2026-12-07. Priya to share harness and runbook by 2026-12-08. Evora to provide trace and prompts by 2026-12-09. Schedule pilot week of 2026-12-14.

[00:19:30] Maya (Evora): Sounds good. Quick question — any gotchas around streaming clients? Our web frontend uses SSE and expects chunks; do you have best practices?

[00:19:50] Priya (Redwood): For SSE we recommend smaller initial chunking to reduce perceived TTFT — e.g., emit first token asap and stream in small batches. We'll test streaming latency and compare with chunked responses.

[00:20:20] Daniel (Evora): What about warm vs cold KV cache? In multi-turn chat we see big improvements after a few turns. Can the benchmark mimic that?

[00:20:40] Priya (Redwood): Yes we can simulate warm cache by replaying complete sessions and measuring successive-turn TTFT. We'll include cold-start scenarios too.

[00:21:10] Ravi (Evora): If Dedicated is required, how long to provision for pilot?

[00:21:25] Samir (Redwood): For Dedicated reserved pool we can provision a small pilot cluster in ~3-7 business days depending on region and capacity; we'll flag capacity when we send the SOW. Private (VPC) takes longer (2-4 weeks) for networking and KMS setup.

[00:22:00] Maya (Evora): On model quantization — does Redwood move models between quantized and fp16 automatically? We want to understand quality vs perf tradeoffs.

[00:22:20] Priya (Redwood): We'll test model variants: quantized int8/gguf vs fp16. We'll report generation quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE or eval prompts) alongside latency. If quality regressions appear we'll show rollout options like A/B or canary.

[00:23:00] Daniel (Evora): Any recommended p95/p99 thresholds you suggest for us to promise in product? We don't want to overpromise to customers.

[00:23:20] Priya (Redwood): For customer-facing promises, p95 TTFT < 300ms and p99 < 800ms is conservative on Hosted for mixed traffic; Dedicated can get you down to p95 < 200-250ms and p99 < 450-500ms for short chat. But we'll validate with your traces.

[00:24:00] Samir (Redwood): Let's capture unknowns: 1) exact sample traces shape, 2) model version you want tested, 3) region preference, 4) whether we should simulate concurrency from multiple geo locations.

[00:24:25] Daniel (Evora): Region preference is US-West for now; we might expand to EU next quarter. We'll send model list — likely smaller 7B and a 13B.

[00:24:50] Priya (Redwood): For the benchmark harness we'll include parameters: replay QPS multiplier (1x, 1.5x), run length, warm-up, batching config toggle, streaming vs non-streaming, and the model variants.

[00:25:20] Maya (Evora): During the POC can we get logs that show request ids and timings so we can correlate to our telemetry?

[00:25:40] Priya (Redwood): Yes — we'll provide per-request JSON with request_id, timestamps for ingress/first-byte/last-byte, batch id, model, hardware profile.

[00:26:00] Daniel (Evora): Great. I want to raise a potential blocker — if p99 is still too high on Hosted, what's the incremental cost to move to Dedicated and what's the impact on throughput?

[00:26:20] Samir (Redwood): We'll include cost-per-token delta and provisioning estimates in the SOW. Dedicated tends to reduce variability (lower p99) and gives higher sustained throughput due to reserved compute and larger batch windows if desired.

[00:27:00] Ravi (Evora): One more ops question: retention of logs. We need 90-day retention; is that by default?

[00:27:15] Priya (Redwood): Default retention is 30 days for standard plan; we can enable 90 days as an add-on for Dedicated/Private. We'll include retention options in the pricing doc.

[00:28:00] Samir (Redwood): Anything else folks want to cover?

[00:28:15] Maya (Evora): Quick check: will you run tests during business hours to mimic real tail conditions?

[00:28:35] Priya (Redwood): We'll coordinate. For initial runs we'll schedule during a low-risk window but we can mimic peak patterns. Also we'll share the raw metrics and dashboards so you can re-run locally.

[00:29:00] Daniel (Evora): OK good. Let's recap next steps.

[00:29:15] Samir (Redwood): Recap: Samir send SOW/pricing Monday 12/07; Priya send harness/runbook 12/08; Evora send traces and prompts 12/09; schedule pilot week of 12/14; Redwood to provide SOC2 and security docs. We'll run Hosted baseline then Dedicated if needed to meet p99.

[00:29:45] Maya (Evora): Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the trace export to you by 12/09.

[00:30:00] Priya (Redwood): Quick note — for the measurement plan doc I'll include example plots: TTFT CDF, TPOT histograms, batch size vs latency, GPU utilization. That should make the tail behavior visible.

[00:30:35] Daniel (Evora): One last question: how do you handle retries and client-side timeouts? If our front end retries we might artificially inflate p99.

[00:30:55] Priya (Redwood): We recommend idempotency tokens and deduping at the client gateway; the harness will have an option to simulate retries. For p99 we'll exclude artificially generated retries unless they reflect real traffic.

[00:31:20] Samir (Redwood): Any blockers to schedule right now?

[00:31:30] Ravi (Evora): None from infra — we'll prioritize the trace export.

[00:31:45] Maya (Evora): We'll also share 3 eval prompts for quality checks so you can report quality vs perf.

[00:32:00] Priya (Redwood): Perfect. We'll also include guidance on streaming chunk sizes and buffer tuning for your SSE client.

[00:32:30] Daniel (Evora): Thanks all.

[00:33:00] Samir (Redwood): Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items we discussed. Meeting adjourned.

[00:33:15] (end-of-call notes)
- Attachments to be sent: Redwood benchmark harness link (TBD), security docs (SOC2), SOW draft and pricing spreadsheet.
- Expected pilot week: 2026-12-14.

Note: Transcription contains occasional minor mis-hearings; speaker labels approximate.
